candidates.exact_span: Animas River, from Estes Arroyo upstream to the Southern Ute Indian Tribal boundary, a classified segment described in Section 20.6.4.404 NMAC
candidates.computation_change_reason: The reach boundary and cross-reference to 20.6.4.404 NMAC define which classified segment—and thus which numeric water-quality standards and segment-specific requirements—apply to a discharge point; misplacing a facility relative to Estes Arroyo or the tribal boundary would change applicable limits (A) and any monitoring tied to that segment (B).

candidates.exact_span: from the confluence with the San Juan River upstream to Estes Arroyo, a classified segment described in Section 20.6.4.403 NMAC
candidates.computation_change_reason: This alternate Animas River reach is governed by 20.6.4.403 NMAC rather than 20.6.4.404 NMAC; interpreting whether a discharge lies upstream or downstream of Estes Arroyo, or relative to the San Juan confluence, changes which limit set and segment-based monitoring requirements apply (A, B).

candidates.exact_span: San Juan River, a classified segment described from the Navajo Nation Boundary at Hogback to Animas River in Section 20.6.4.401 NMAC in the San Juan River Basin
candidates.computation_change_reason: The San Juan River classified segment and its 20.6.4.401 NMAC reference establish a distinct limit and requirement regime for discharges between Hogback and the Animas confluence; boundary interpretation (Hogback, Animas confluence) affects which numeric limits govern (A) and which segment-conditioned monitoring applies (B).
